CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.claim: The failure is SQLSTATE 42501 raised at trigger execution.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.evidence: P1C verbatim: 'ERROR: 42501: permission denied for schema auth / LINE 1: v_actor := auth.uid() / QUERY: v_actor := auth.uid() / CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function enforce_organization_commercial_acceptance_invariants() line <N> at assignment'.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.THE_BODY_RELATIVE_LINE_IS_NOT_A_SOURCE_C: CORRECTED IN R2 (certification NON_BLOCKING finding). The 'line <N>' PostgreSQL prints is relative to the PL/pgSQL BODY as installed, so it varies with the substrate: the R1 minimal substrate reported line 22 and the R2 canonical reproduction reported line 11 for the SAME statement, because each condensed the DECLARE block differently. Neither is a citation of db/migrations/0072. THE SOURCE ANCHOR IS THE FILE LINE: db/migrations/0072:198, 'v_actor := auth.uid();'. No control may assert a body-relative line number; assert the QUERY text and the function name instead.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.WHY_THE_POLICY_SURVIVES_WHAT_THE_BODY_DO: MEASURED ASYMMETRY, and the single most important finding in this section. The INSERT policy's WITH CHECK contains a DIRECT auth.uid() (0072:116). If THAT expression also required schema USAGE, the defect would not be trigger-scoped and no trigger-scoped remediation could make PG-06 satisfiable. P2A proves it does not: with the trigger disabled and the policy fully armed, the same runtime role in the same identity context inserted successfully. A STORED policy expression was name-resolved at CREATE time and is executed against stored OIDs, so at run time PostgreSQL checks EXECUTE on the function and never re-checks USAGE on the schema. A PL/pgSQL body parses its SQL expressions at RUNTIME in the calling session, so name resolution -- and therefore schema USAGE -- IS checked against the invoker. P8C isolates the other half: after REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION auth.uid() FROM PUBLIC the stored policy fails with '42501: permission denied for function uid'. EXECUTE is what a stored policy needs; USAGE is what a PL/pgSQL body additionally needs.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.CONSEQUENCE_BINDING: The defect is TRIGGER-SCOPED. A remediation confined to the trigger function is SUFFICIENT, and no policy, no grant and no role needs to change.

Granting the OWNER usage on the attacker-writable schema flipped it: with the pin still removed, the shadowed registry WAS used and a FORGED content_digest was accepted and stored, defeating I-T4-4 (P7B, INSERT 0 1 with content_digest sha256:dead...). Restoring the pin refused the identical attack (P7C). CONCLUSION: the pin is the decisive barrier, with the precise precondition that the owner can see a schema the attacker can write to. A second, independent barrier was also measured: the runtime role holds no CREATE on schema public (P6A, has_schema_privilege(app,public,CREATE)=f). Both are real; neither is a reason to omit the other.
